html:
Nickel ore was found in New Caledonia in 1864 by the engineer Jules Garnier, and mining began soon after. The island holds one of the largest nickel reserves in the world.

The company Le Nickel was founded in 1880, and miners were brought from Asia, among them Japanese, Javanese and Vietnamese workers. Nickel booms in the 1960s drew migrants from France, Wallis and Futuna and Tahiti, changing the balance of the population.

Control of nickel became part of the independence deal: the Matignon and Nouméa accords gave the Kanak-led north its own smelter. Falling prices in the 2020s closed plants and fed the unrest of 2024.
